articleTitle: Spectral properties of radar sea clutter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Examines the properties of high range resolution radar sea clutter spectra with reference to those properties observed non-coherently. In particular it is demonstrated how the nonGaussian characteristics of noncoherently detected clutter manifest themselves in the spectral domain and how these characteristics require a thorough understanding in order to optimise any detection processing. Further, it is shown how the properties of the clutter spectra vary with transmit and receive polarisation and how this should lead to an improved insight into the mechanisms responsible for experimental observations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Physical mechanisms associated with the compound K-distribution sea clutter model
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Discusses how the 1980s has seen significant advances in the characterisation and analysis of the statistical properties of sea clutter and its influence on the performance of high resolution maritime radar systems based on the K distribution. The authors present a preliminary investigation of the consequences of a more detailed theory, making particular reference to experimental data and to the simple physical pictures which are believed to underlie the success of the K distribution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of neural-network and model-based texture classification
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Addresses the problem of the classification of clutter textures in coherent imaging, e.g. synthetic aperture radar. The major difficulty of such classification lies in defining a model by which the image may be interpreted. Progress has been made in representing such clutter textures in terms of correlated K-distributed noise. An alternative approach which is non-committal about the form of the texture is to use neural network methods which learn the underlying model from training data. The authors compare the performance of a neural network approach with a model-based one used for the classification of artificial textures generated using a correlated K-distribution noise model. This serves as a calibration of the neural network in well-characterised circumstances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Millimetric radar clutter measurements from desert surfaces
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Describes millimetric data gathering trials carried out by British Aerospace and Edinburgh University over a varied range of desert terrains. An initial reconnaissance survey located 8 sites giving maximum variability of topography and rock or surface sediment. Subsequently, a detailed programme of field recording and analysis was carried out during 22 days of field trials in Autumn 1987. One of the principal aims of the trial was to make a detailed investigation into the correlation between radar reflectivity and ground conditions over desert surfaces. Radar reflectivity was measured over a range of depression angles using an airborne W-band radar. These measurements were supported with aerial photography and detailed ground truth study. A description of the airborne and ground data gathering procedures is given together with a brief indication of the data analysis. This is followed by an investigation into the correlation between backscatter measurements and ground truth parameters and modelling of the backscatter returns using both physical and empirical models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generation of synthetic clutter maps for millimetric radar modelling
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Easams have been working with RSRE on the modelling of millimetric radar sensors. The aim of the work to investigate how a scanning airborne millimetric radar sensor can pick out a stationary tank against a background of land clutter. Only the worst case of a stationary tank has been considered. Recent activities have concentrated on dual polarisation sensors. As well as generating clutter maps, Easams have also written a simulation, called MIDAS, which uses these maps to calculate the signals received by sensor. Associated software has also been written to process this calculated signal to investigate the problem of distinguishing between tanks and clutter spikes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Temporal and spatial characteristics of I-band multipath propagation over the sea
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: The study of forward scatter from the sea surface is of importance in several applications of radar operated at low elevation angles over the sea, in which severe fading can occur due to multipath propagation. Extensive work has been done on the tracking accuracy against low flying targets, of a radar near a rough surface, to predict the angular accuracy of the radar measurement on what is assumed to be a point target. This work treats only the single point amplitude statistics of the multipath phenomena although the derivation of the statistics involves consideration of a glistening surface. It should be noted that temporal or spatial elements are not included in the model. In order to investigate the temporal and spatial multipath effects a programme of full scale measurements, using cliff-top radars is underway, allowing the phenomenon of forward scattering to be investigated in a relatively controlled manner. The latest results of the spatial decorrelation in the horizontal and vertical directions are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A coherent model of radar weather clutter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Considers a coherent model of radar weather clutter which is based on the analysis of digitally recorded radar data. Representative models of radar clutter are a necessary prerequisite for the design of radar signal processors, since a major task of such processors is to suppress clutter returns. In the design of a coherent signal processor, the Doppler spectrum of the clutter returns is of prime importance. However, it is also recognised that in order to fix thresholds to govern the false alarm rate, the degree of spatial variability or 'spikiness' in the clutter must be taken into account. This is almost always achieved by invoking a separate, entirely empirical model of the spatial fluctuations. It is shown how a single coherent model of weather clutter can be constructed, which combines both the Doppler spectra and the spatial variability of the clutter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Considers the simple back reflection geometries which are generalised to take account of finite target size and roughness, and different types of diffuser, illumination and imaging geometries. The phenomenology so established is applicable to a wide variety of active remote sensing systems. Bearing in mind that optical physicists rarely observe in the back-scattering direction whilst radar engineers rarely do otherwise, it would appear prudent in situations where multiple scattering may occur, to check its magnitude in case re-assessment of system performance is necessary.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gross spatial structure of land clutter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: If the two detection probabilities (per scan in cluttered and uncluttered regions) are very different then the path of an air vehicle is critical in determining the radar performance. Simplistic smooth earth, uniform sigma degrees clutter models are totally inadequate to describe such cases. The authors develop a more realistic representation of the spatial distribution of land clutter. This would complement the study of small-scale characteristics such as texture, by describing whether or not a given resolution cell (or group of cells) should be treated as cluttered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Empirical models for radar performance prediction in sea clutter
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Briefly reviews some of the available empirical models for clutter and presents some new results for approximating detection performance in K-distributed sea clutter. The emphasis is on clutter observed at low grazing angles and high range resolution, where significant deviations from Gaussian amplitude statistics are observed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-resolution multi-frequency analysis of high range resolution sea reflections
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: A description of the surface by a K distribution is of particular interest in that the K distribution can be decomposed into a Rayleigh distributed fast fluctuating amplitude component modulated by a chi distributed slow fluctuating amplitude component. Thus if the observed data can be described by a K distribution the components of the return can be analysed separately and related to physical aspects of the sea surface. The slow correlation characteristics of the backscatter can then be included in target detection strategies and radar performance calculations. Failure to allow for the correlation characteristics can lead to large errors in radar detection performance and radar false alarm rate. Agreement with a K distribution model has been demonstrated for a limited range of radar parameters. The K model has been shown to be valid at I Band and resolutions down to 4 m. The author describes measurements and analyses performed at the Marconi Research Centre to extend the observations to higher resolutions and a range of frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent developments in propagation forecasting: channel characterisation for radar systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Radar Clutter and Multipath Propagation
abstract: Presents a parabolic equation likely to displace mode and ray methods for the modelling of clear-air propagation in the troposphere. A PC based forecasting model has been developed which is more efficient than either of these earlier approaches. Radar coverage diagrams of antennas in arbitrary refractive index structures are easily generated. This new tool enables the effect of the propagation channel on radar system performance to be investigated. Complex problems, including multipath and ducting, and the frequency selective effects of these on short pulse radars, can now be tackled quantitatively for the first time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
